heading: EXT. FROZEN MOUNTAIN LAKE - ICE SHELF - DAY

units.text: EXT. FROZEN MOUNTAIN LAKE - ICE SHELF - DAY
Pale sun.
No wind.
A wide white plain, scored with old snowmobile tracks.
At its edge, a crude fishing hut of plywood and tarp, a stovepipe giving off a lazy ribbon of smoke.
Five snowmobiles lie crossways in the snow.
Five people crouch around a hole in the ice, lines dropped into black water.
HARLAN COOPER (50s, guide, patched down jacket) hums, jigging his rod.
BEATRICE "BEA" LINDQVIST (30s, photographer, bright red hat) frames a shot with her thumbs.
KOJI NAKAGAWA (40s, geologist, notebook strapped to his chest) taps the ice with a steel probe.
PRIYA RAMASWAMY (20s, student, oversized mittens) holds a thermos with both hands.
And OSCAR BELL (60s, retired pilot, silent, cigar unlit in his teeth) leans against his snowmobile, watching the sky.
That's a good day, folks. Look at this. No wind, no crowd, no rush.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: It's too quiet.
units.name: BEA

units.text: Quiet is why you pay me.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: I like it.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Ice here's thirty inches. Good.
units.name: KOJI

units.text: He taps again.
Frowns.
Taps a third place and listens, head tilted.
No one else notices.
Priya, pour me one.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: It's still hot.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: She pours.
Harlan takes it, sips, nods in approval.
Oscar lifts one hand to shade his eyes.
Harlan.
units.name: OSCAR

units.text: Yeah?
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: How long's the lake been this still?
units.name: OSCAR

units.text: Since December.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: That's not what I asked.
units.name: OSCAR

units.text: Harlan glances at him.
A flicker.
Then he looks away and takes another sip.
You worry too much, Oscar.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Bea lowers her camera and walks a few steps away across the ice, her red hat bobbing.
Koji stays crouched, his probe sunk to the hilt in the snow.
Priya follows Bea, thermos steaming.
Harlan sets down his cup.
Oscar takes the cigar from his teeth.
A soft sound.
A long, low note, felt more than heard, like someone drawing a bow across the planet.
Everyone stops.
Priya's thermos slips from her hand and bounces.
Bea turns slowly.
Koji lifts his head.
Harlan stands.
Oscar does not move, only watches Harlan.
That's the shelf.
units.name: KOJI

units.text: It's the lake settling. It does that.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Not in March. Not at thirty inches.
units.name: KOJI

units.text: Everybody stay calm and walk to the snowmobiles. One at a time. Do not run.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Nobody runs.
The five of them move across the white at a measured pace, like people leaving a church.
Bea's boots squeak.
Priya's mittens hang from their strings.
Koji walks backwards, eyes on the ice.
A CRACK, then another, racing from the fishing hole in a black spiderweb.
Water wells up between the lines.
Go!
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Now they run.
Harlan grabs Priya under the arms and swings her toward the nearest machine.
Bea scrambles on behind Koji, camera banging against his back.
Oscar is already on his snowmobile, engine roaring, and he does not wait; he guns it across the white, sled slewing, then wheels in a wide arc and comes back for the others.
The hut TILTS and slides sideways into the lake, stovepipe still smoking, plywood groaning, and goes down with a gulp.
Harlan, white-faced, kicks his engine to life.
Koji hauls Priya aboard behind him.
Bea clings to Koji.
They roar toward the shore in a ragged line, snow spraying, Oscar leading, with the whole sheet of ice behind them breaking into slow plates.
On the bank, they skid to a halt and turn.
The place where they stood is open water, steaming in the cold.
A single red mitten floats in it.
Priya looks at her bare hand.
Then at Harlan.
Then at the mitten.
You said it was thirty inches.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Harlan opens his mouth.
Closes it.
Oscar puts the cigar back between his teeth and lights it at last, his hands steady, his eyes on nobody.
